name: Measurement of the very rare K+ -> pi+ nu nubar decay
title: Measurement of the very rare K+ -> pi+ nu nubar decay

date.note: date is the arXiv preprint submission date; publication is JHEP06(2021)093.

claim.quote: Measurement of the very rare K+ -> pi+ nu nubar decay

summary.plain: NA62's first solid measurement of how often a positive kaon decays into a pion and two invisible neutrinos, using data from 2016 to 2018 -- one of the rarest decays ever measured, though the result was not yet precise enough to call an observation.
summary.technical: Branching-ratio measurement of K+ -> pi+ nu nubar from the 2016-2018 NA62 Run 1 data set: BR = (10.6+4.0-3.4|stat +- 0.9syst) x 10^-11 at 68% CL, based on 20 signal candidates with an expected background of 7.0 events, corresponding to 3.4 sigma significance.

why_it_matters: K+ -> pi+ nu nubar is one of the theoretically cleanest rare kaon decays for probing physics beyond the Standard Model via the CKM matrix element |Vtd|; this 2021 result was NA62's first branching-ratio measurement of the decay at evidence level, ahead of the 2025 observation.

key_value.note: Branching ratio in units of 10^-11; stored as a bare count-like number because the ontology has no branching-ratio dimension. See key_value_text for the fully formatted value.

key_value_text.value: BR(K+ -> pi+ nu nubar) = (10.6+4.0-3.4|stat +- 0.9syst) x 10^-11, based on 20 signal candidates with an expected background of 7.0 events
